questions.question: Find $\displaystyle\int \frac{1}{1+4x^2}\,dx$.
questions.answer: Write $\dfrac{1}{1+4x^2}=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{2}{1+(2x)^2}$, so the integral is $\dfrac12\tan^{-1}2x+c$ (B).

questions.question: It is given that $\cos x=\dfrac23$, where $0<x<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. What is the value of $\cos 2x$?
questions.answer: $\cos2x=2\cos^2x-1=2\left(\dfrac49\right)-1=-\dfrac19$ (A).

questions.question: A discrete random variable $X$ is binomially distributed with a mean of $6$ and a variance of $1.5$. What is the number of independent trials?
The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown, and it is transformed to give the graph of $y=g(x)$, also shown. What transformation was applied?
questions.answer: $g$ is even, and for $x>0$ it copies the part of $f$ at $-x$ (e.g. $g(1)=f(-1)=1$), so $g(x)=f(-|x|)$ (C). Option A equals $f(|x|)$, which would give $g(1)=f(1)=-2$. Options B and D involve square roots/squares of $f$, which are not defined where $f$ has the wrong sign, or do not give the graph.

questions.question: Which diagram best represents the solution set of $\dfrac{2}{3-x}\le 1$?
questions.answer: Multiply by $(3-x)^2>0$: $2(3-x)\le(3-x)^2\Rightarrow(3-x)(2-(3-x))\le0\Rightarrow(3-x)(x-1)\le0$, i.e. $(x-3)(x-1)\ge0$ with $x\ne3$. So $x\le1$ or $x>3$ (B).

questions.question: Which of the following is the simplest expression for $\dfrac{\cos4\theta}{\sin2\theta}+\dfrac{\sin4\theta}{\cos2\theta}$?
questions.answer: Common denominator: $\dfrac{\cos4\theta\cos2\theta+\sin4\theta\sin2\theta}{\sin2\theta\cos2\theta}=\dfrac{\cos(4\theta-2\theta)}{\sin2\theta\cos2\theta}=\dfrac{\cos2\theta}{\sin2\theta\cos2\theta}=\dfrac1{\sin2\theta}=\operatorname{cosec}2\theta$ (D).

questions.question: The line $y=3x-4$ is tangential to the graph of $y=f(x)$ at the point where $x=1$. Assuming $y=f(x)$ is invertible, what is the equation of the normal to the graph of $y=f^{-1}(x)$ at the point where $x=-1$?
questions.answer: From the tangent, $f(1)=3(1)-4=-1$ and $f'(1)=3$. So $f^{-1}(-1)=1$: the point $(-1,1)$ lies on $y=f^{-1}(x)$, with gradient $\dfrac{1}{f'(1)}=\dfrac13$. The normal has gradient $-3$: $y-1=-3(x+1)$, so $y=-3x-2$ (C).

questions.question: In how many ways can the letters of the word DIFFERENT be arranged in a row with the Fs separated?
questions.answer: DIFFERENT has 9 letters with two Fs and two Es. All arrangements: $\dfrac{9!}{2!\,2!}=90\,720$. Arrangements with the Fs together (treat FF as one block): $\dfrac{8!}{2!}=20\,160$. Fs separated: $90\,720-20\,160=70\,560$ (B).

questions.question: The general solution to a differential equation is $f(x)=\ln(e^x+c)$, where $c$ is a constant. Which of the following best represents the direction field for the differential equation?
questions.answer: With $y=\ln(e^x+c)$ we have $e^y=e^x+c$, so $c=e^y-e^x$, and $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{e^x}{e^x+c}=\dfrac{e^x}{e^y}=e^{x-y}$. The slope depends on $x-y$: it equals $1$ along $y=x$, is steep (near vertical) where $y<x$ (below the line) and is nearly horizontal where $y>x$ (above the line). This is diagram D.

questions.question: The temperature of a pastry, $T^\circ$C, is monitored after it is placed into an oven set to a temperature of $160^\circ$C. It is assumed that $T=160-Ae^{-kt}$, where $A$ and $k$ are constants, and $t$ is the time in minutes after the pastry was placed in the oven. A recording shows that the pastry reaches $100^\circ$C after $t=10$ minutes and the linear rate of change in the temperature at that time would mean it reaches $160^\circ$C when $t=25$ minutes, as shown (graph not to scale). What is the value of $k$?
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=kAe^{-kt}=k(160-T)$. At $t=10$, $T=100$, so the gradient is $60k$. The tangent passes through $(10,100)$ and $(25,160)$, so its gradient is $\dfrac{160-100}{25-10}=4$. Hence $60k=4$ and $k=\dfrac1{15}$ (C).

questions.question: A mathematics class consists of 4 girls and 4 boys. A committee of 5 students must be formed. Find the number of different committees that can be formed.
A mathematics class consists of 4 girls and 4 boys. A committee of 5 students is formed (there are 56 possible committees). Find the probability that there are more girls than boys on the committee.
questions.answer:
More girls than boys means 3 girls and 2 boys, or 4 girls and 1 boy.
$\binom43\binom42+\binom44\binom41=4\times6+1\times4=28$.
$$P=\frac{28}{56}=\frac12.$$

questions.question: Let $f(x)=2\sin x+6\cos x+13$, for $0\le x\le2\pi$. Write $2\sin x+6\cos x$ in the form $R\sin(x+\alpha)$, where $R>0$ and $\alpha$ is acute.
questions.answer:
$R\sin(x+\alpha)=R\sin x\cos\alpha+R\cos x\sin\alpha$, so $R\cos\alpha=2$ and $R\sin\alpha=6$.
$R=\sqrt{2^2+6^2}=\sqrt{40}=2\sqrt{10}$ and $\tan\alpha=3$, so $\alpha=\tan^{-1}3$.
$$2\sin x+6\cos x=2\sqrt{10}\sin\left(x+\tan^{-1}3\right).$$

questions.question: Let $f(x)=2\sin x+6\cos x+13$, for $0\le x\le2\pi$, so that $f(x)=2\sqrt{10}\sin\left(x+\tan^{-1}3\right)+13$. Show that $$\frac1{13+\sqrt{40}}\le\frac1{f(x)}\le\frac1{13-\sqrt{40}}.$$
questions.answer:
Since $-1\le\sin(x+\tan^{-1}3)\le1$ and $2\sqrt{10}=\sqrt{40}$, we have $13-\sqrt{40}\le f(x)\le13+\sqrt{40}$.
Both bounds are positive ($13>\sqrt{40}$), so $f(x)>0$ and taking reciprocals reverses the inequalities:
$$\frac1{13+\sqrt{40}}\le\frac1{f(x)}\le\frac1{13-\sqrt{40}}.$$
The minimum of $\frac1{f(x)}$ occurs when $\sin(\cdot)=1$ and the maximum when $\sin(\cdot)=-1$, as required.

questions.question: Find the coefficient of $x^5$ in the expansion of $(1+3x)^2(1+x)^7$.
questions.answer:
$(1+3x)^2=1+6x+9x^2$. The $x^5$ terms come from $1\cdot\binom75x^5$, $6x\cdot\binom74x^4$ and $9x^2\cdot\binom73x^3$:
$$\binom75+6\binom74+9\binom73=21+6(35)+9(35)=21+210+315=546.$$

questions.question: Given that $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf{u}=\begin{pmatrix}-3\\2\end{pmatrix}$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf{v}=\begin{pmatrix}5\\-3\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{w}=\overrightarrow{AB}$, find $\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{w}$.
questions.answer:
$\mathbf{w}=\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}=\begin{pmatrix}8\\-5\end{pmatrix}$.
$\mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{v}=8(5)+(-5)(-3)=55$ and $|\mathbf{v}|^2=25+9=34$.
$$\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{w}=\frac{\mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{v}|^2}\mathbf{v}=\frac{55}{34}\begin{pmatrix}5\\-3\end{pmatrix}.$$

questions.question: Use the substitution $u=\sin^2x$ to evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/3}\frac{\sin2x}{1+\sin^2x}\,dx$, leaving your final answer in the form $\ln\dfrac ab$.
questions.answer:
$u=\sin^2x\Rightarrow du=2\sin x\cos x\,dx=\sin2x\,dx$.
When $x=\frac\pi4$, $u=\frac12$; when $x=\frac\pi3$, $u=\frac34$.
$$\int_{1/2}^{3/4}\frac{du}{1+u}=\Big[\ln|1+u|\Big]_{1/2}^{3/4}=\ln\frac74-\ln\frac32=\ln\frac{7}{6}.$$

questions.question: Use mathematical induction to prove that $13\times6^n+2$ is divisible by 5 for all integers $n\ge1$.
questions.answer:
**Step 1 (n = 1).** $13\times6+2=80=5\times16$, which is divisible by 5. True for $n=1$.
**Step 2.** Assume true for $n=k$: $13\times6^k+2=5M$ for some integer $M$, i.e. $13\times6^k=5M-2$.
Prove true for $n=k+1$:
$$13\times6^{k+1}+2=6(13\times6^k)+2=6(5M-2)+2=30M-10=5(6M-2),$$
which is divisible by 5 since $6M-2$ is an integer.
**Step 3.** True for $n=1$, and if true for $n=k$ then true for $n=k+1$; so by the principle of mathematical induction it is true for all integers $n\ge1$.

questions.question: It is known that an Olympic archer has an $80\%$ chance of hitting the bullseye. What is the minimum number of shots that must be attempted for the probability of hitting a bullseye exactly 9 times to be higher than the probability of hitting the bullseye exactly 8 times?
questions.answer:
Let $X\sim\text{Bin}(n,0.8)$. We need $P(X=9)>P(X=8)$:
$$\binom n9(0.8)^9(0.2)^{n-9}>\binom n8(0.8)^8(0.2)^{n-8}.$$
Divide by $(0.8)^8(0.2)^{n-9}$ and use $\binom n9\big/\binom n8=\dfrac{n-8}{9}$:
$$\frac{n-8}{9}(0.8)>0.2\Rightarrow n-8>\frac{9}{4}\Rightarrow n>10.25.$$
The minimum number of shots is $11$.

questions.question: Using $t=\tan\dfrac x2$, solve the equation $5\sin x-12\cos x=5$ for $-\pi\le x\le\pi$, giving answers correct to two decimal places where necessary.
questions.answer:
With $\sin x=\dfrac{2t}{1+t^2}$ and $\cos x=\dfrac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}$:
$$10t-12(1-t^2)=5(1+t^2)\Rightarrow 7t^2+10t-17=0\Rightarrow(t-1)(7t+17)=0,$$
so $t=1$ or $t=-\dfrac{17}{7}$.
Since $-\frac\pi2\le\frac x2\le\frac\pi2$: $\tan\frac x2=1\Rightarrow x=\dfrac\pi2$, and $\tan\frac x2=-\frac{17}7\Rightarrow x=-2\tan^{-1}\frac{17}{7}\approx-2.36$.
$$x=\frac\pi2\ \text{ or }\ x\approx-2.36.$$ (Check: $x=\pi$ gives $5\sin\pi-12\cos\pi=12\ne5$, so no solution is lost.)

questions.question: The region enclosed by the curve $y=\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2x+1}}$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=1$ and $x=a$ is shaded (see diagram). When the shaded region is rotated about the $x$-axis, the solid generated has a volume of $\pi\ln\dfrac{64}{27}$ units$^3$. Find the exact value of $a$.
questions.answer:
$$V=\pi\int_1^a\frac{3}{2x+1}\,dx=\frac{3\pi}{2}\Big[\ln(2x+1)\Big]_1^a=\frac{3\pi}2\ln\frac{2a+1}{3}.$$
Set equal to $\pi\ln\frac{64}{27}$: $\ln\dfrac{2a+1}3=\dfrac23\ln\dfrac{64}{27}=\ln\left(\dfrac{64}{27}\right)^{2/3}=\ln\dfrac{16}{9}$.
So $\dfrac{2a+1}{3}=\dfrac{16}9$, $2a+1=\dfrac{16}{3}$, giving $$a=\frac{13}{6}.$$

questions.question: When a polynomial $P(x)$ is divided by $(x-2)(x+1)$ it gives a remainder of $x-b$. When this polynomial is divided by $x+1$, it gives a remainder of $3$. What is the value of $b$?
questions.answer:
$P(x)=(x-2)(x+1)Q(x)+x-b$. By the remainder theorem $P(-1)=3$:
$$3=0+(-1)-b\Rightarrow b=-4.$$

questions.question: The area of a sector $ABC$ with a radius of $r$ metres and an angle $\theta$ radians at the centre $A$ is increasing at a rate of $5\ \text{m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$ while $\theta$ remains constant. At what rate is the radius $r$ increasing when the arc length of the sector is $20$ m?
questions.answer:
$A=\frac12r^2\theta\Rightarrow\dfrac{dA}{dr}=r\theta$. The arc length is $\ell=r\theta$, so $\dfrac{dA}{dr}=\ell$.
$$\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac{dA}{dr}\cdot\frac{dr}{dt}\Rightarrow5=20\frac{dr}{dt}\Rightarrow\frac{dr}{dt}=0.25.$$
The radius is increasing at $0.25$ m/s.

questions.question: In the diagram, $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ are unit vectors that intersect at an angle of $2\theta$. Express $|\mathbf a+\mathbf b|^2$ in terms of $\cos\theta$.
questions.answer:
$$|\mathbf a+\mathbf b|^2=(\mathbf a+\mathbf b)\cdot(\mathbf a+\mathbf b)=|\mathbf a|^2+2\,\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b+|\mathbf b|^2=1+2\cos2\theta+1.$$
So $|\mathbf a+\mathbf b|^2=2+2(2\cos^2\theta-1)=4\cos^2\theta$.

questions.question: If $f(x)=f^{-1}(x)$, then the function $f(x)$ is said to be *self-inverse* for all $x$ in the domain. Let $f(x)=\dfrac{3x-5}{x+k}$. Find the value of $k$ so that $f(x)$ is self-inverse.
questions.answer:
Let $y=\dfrac{3x-5}{x+k}$. Swap variables: $x=\dfrac{3y-5}{y+k}\Rightarrow xy+kx=3y-5\Rightarrow y(x-3)=-kx-5$, so $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{-kx-5}{x-3}=\dfrac{kx+5}{3-x}$.
Self-inverse: $\dfrac{3x-5}{x+k}=\dfrac{kx+5}{3-x}$, so $(3x-5)(3-x)=(kx+5)(x+k)$:
$$-3x^2+14x-15=kx^2+(k^2+5)x+5k.$$
Comparing $x^2$ coefficients: $k=-3$. Check: $k^2+5=14$ and $5k=-15$. 
$$k=-3.$$

questions.question: A curve is defined parametrically by $x=\cos(\sin^{-1}t)$, $y=\sin(\sin^{-1}t)$, where $0\le t\le1$. Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=0$.
questions.answer:
For $0\le t\le1$, $\sin(\sin^{-1}t)=t$ and $\cos(\sin^{-1}t)=\sqrt{1-t^2}$. So $x=\sqrt{1-t^2}$, $y=t$.
$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac{-t}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=1$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\sqrt{1-t^2}}{-t}$.
At $t=0$ the point is $(1,0)$ and $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=0$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=1\ne0$: the gradient is undefined, so the tangent is vertical.
$$x=1.$$ (Alternatively, $x^2+y^2=1$ with $y\ge0$ is a unit semicircle, whose tangent at $(1,0)$ is $x=1$.)

questions.question: The region enclosed by the graph of $y=\tan^{-1}x$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=1$ and $x=\sqrt3$ is shaded (see diagram; the curve passes through $\left(1,\frac\pi4\right)$ and $\left(\sqrt3,\frac\pi3\right)$). Find the area of the shaded region, leaving your answer in exact form.
questions.answer:
Area $=\displaystyle\int_1^{\sqrt3}\tan^{-1}x\,dx$. This equals the rectangle $[0,\sqrt3]\times[0,\frac\pi3]$ minus the rectangle $[0,1]\times[0,\frac\pi4]$ minus the area between $x=\tan y$ and the $y$-axis for $\frac\pi4\le y\le\frac\pi3$:
$$A=\frac{\pi\sqrt3}{3}-\frac\pi4-\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/3}\tan y\,dy.$$
$\displaystyle\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/3}\tan y\,dy=\Big[-\ln|\cos y|\Big]_{\pi/4}^{\pi/3}=-\ln\frac12+\ln\frac1{\sqrt2}=\ln2-\frac12\ln2=\frac12\ln2$.
$$A=\frac{\pi\sqrt3}{3}-\frac\pi4-\frac12\ln2=\frac{4\pi\sqrt3-3\pi-6\ln2}{12}.$$

questions.question: The diagram shows a triangle $ABD$ with $C$ on $BD$, where $\overrightarrow{AD}=\mathbf a$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}=\mathbf b$. Given that $5\overrightarrow{BD}=6\overrightarrow{CD}$, prove that $\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf a-6\mathbf b$.
questions.answer:
$\overrightarrow{BD}=\overrightarrow{BC}+\overrightarrow{CD}=\mathbf b+\overrightarrow{CD}$. Substituting into $5\overrightarrow{BD}=6\overrightarrow{CD}$:
$$5\mathbf b+5\overrightarrow{CD}=6\overrightarrow{CD}\Rightarrow\overrightarrow{CD}=5\mathbf b.$$
So $\overrightarrow{BD}=\mathbf b+5\mathbf b=6\mathbf b$.
$$\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{AD}+\overrightarrow{DB}=\mathbf a-6\mathbf b.$$

questions.question: Use the substitution $x=\sin\theta$, for $-\dfrac\pi2<\theta<\dfrac\pi2$, to solve the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y\sqrt{1-x^2}$ where $-1<x<1$, given that $y=2$ when $x=0$.
questions.answer:
Separate variables: $\displaystyle\int\frac{dy}{y}=\int\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx$.
With $x=\sin\theta$, $dx=\cos\theta\,d\theta$ and $\sqrt{1-x^2}=\cos\theta$ (as $\cos\theta>0$):
$$\int\cos^2\theta\,d\theta=\frac12\int(1+\cos2\theta)\,d\theta=\frac\theta2+\frac{\sin2\theta}{4}+C.$$
So $\ln|y|=\dfrac{\theta}{2}+\dfrac{\sin\theta\cos\theta}{2}+C=\dfrac{\sin^{-1}x+x\sqrt{1-x^2}}{2}+C$.
When $x=0$, $y=2$: $\ln2=C$.
$$y=2\exp\left(\frac{\sin^{-1}x+x\sqrt{1-x^2}}{2}\right).$$

questions.question: A particle is projected from the origin with initial speed $v_0$ m/s at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. The velocity vector at time $t$ after projection is $\mathbf v(t)=\begin{pmatrix}v_0\cos\theta\\v_0\sin\theta-gt\end{pmatrix}$ (do not prove this). The speed of the projectile is half of the initial speed when it is at a vertical height of $H$ metres above the horizontal. Show that $H=\dfrac{3v_0^2}{8g}$.
questions.answer:
Speed $=\tfrac12v_0$ means $|\mathbf v|^2=\tfrac14v_0^2$:
$$v_0^2\cos^2\theta+(v_0\sin\theta-gt)^2=\tfrac14v_0^2\Rightarrow v_0^2-2v_0gt\sin\theta+g^2t^2=\tfrac14v_0^2,$$
so $g^2t^2=2v_0gt\sin\theta-\tfrac34v_0^2\quad(1)$.
Integrating the vertical velocity (with $y=0$ at $t=0$): $y=v_0t\sin\theta-\tfrac12gt^2$. At this time $y=H$, and by (1) $\tfrac12gt^2=\dfrac{1}{2g}\left(2v_0gt\sin\theta-\tfrac34v_0^2\right)=v_0t\sin\theta-\dfrac{3v_0^2}{8g}$. Hence
$$H=v_0t\sin\theta-\left(v_0t\sin\theta-\frac{3v_0^2}{8g}\right)=\frac{3v_0^2}{8g}.$$

questions.question: A particle is projected from the origin with initial speed $v_0$ m/s at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, with velocity $\mathbf v(t)=\begin{pmatrix}v_0\cos\theta\\v_0\sin\theta-gt\end{pmatrix}$. The speed of the projectile equals half of its initial speed, $\tfrac12v_0$, exactly when $g^2t^2-2v_0g\sin\theta\,t+\tfrac34v_0^2=0$. If the speed of the projectile is half of its initial speed only once during its flight, find the value of $\theta$.
questions.answer:
The quadratic in $t$ has exactly one solution when its discriminant is zero:
$$(2v_0g\sin\theta)^2-4g^2\cdot\tfrac34v_0^2=0\Rightarrow4\sin^2\theta=3\Rightarrow\sin\theta=\frac{\sqrt3}2$$
(taking $0<\theta<\frac\pi2$ as an angle of projection). Therefore $$\theta=\frac\pi3\ (60^\circ).$$ (This is when the speed is half of $v_0$ only at the top of the flight, where $v=v_0\cos\theta=\frac12v_0$.)
